description: We’re a curious and creative team passionate about exploration, technology, and software development. We love turning ideas into practical solutions, and we’re currently building a smart app that helps people stay alert and prepared for natural disasters.
summary:
Safe Horizon is an intelligent emergency response and planetary monitoring platform built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. The platform bridges the critical gap between complex aerospace data and human safety during global crises.
By directly synthesizing live satellite telemetry from NASA’s EONET API and analyzing localized climate signals—including precipitation, temperature anomalies, and environmental vectors—Safe Horizon delivers actionable threat intelligence in real time. The interface features a dynamic interactive World Map alongside an advanced graphical Heatmap layer that tracks environmental anomalies, giving citizens and first responders immediate visibility into disaster zones.
Engineered with universal inclusivity at its core, Safe Horizon features a runtime structural Multilingual framework (Arabic layout with full native RTL remapping) to guarantee flawless communication under crisis. Furthermore, to ensure uninterrupted readability under extreme field environments or vision deficiencies, the mapping layers integrate WCAG-compliant Colorblind Accessibility modes (Deuteranopia/Protanopia remapping and Monochrome layers). Safe Horizon transforms cold satellite data into a universally accessible, life-saving beacon for global humanitarian resilience.
details:
Safe Horizon is an intelligent, real-time interactive emergency response platform designed to democratize complex planetary data and save human lives during climate crises. Powered by modern web technologies—including React 19, Vite, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS—the platform continuously fetches live telemetry from NASA’s EONET API alongside localized MERRA-2 climate datasets. It dynamically visualizes these threats using an interactive World Map and a highly descriptive graphical Heatmap layer, allowing first responders and citizens to immediately identify critical disaster zones.

The true creativity and social impact of Safe Horizon lie in its strict adherence to human-centered inclusive engineering. Recognizing that high-stress evacuation scenarios demand absolute visual clarity, the team prioritized universal accessibility. The platform considerations include an explicit runtime Multilingual framework that instantaneously remaps the layout to a native Arabic Right-to-Left (RTL) typography without breaking interface design. Furthermore, to protect individuals with Color Vision Deficiency (CVD) or navigating low-light survival environments, the system features WCAG-compliant Colorblind Accessibility modes that remap dangerous red-green variables into an optimized Blue/Amber high-contrast layer.

Ultimately, Safe Horizon serves as a universal lifeline. By integrating an automatic location-detecting Global SOS Directory covering 250 countries, it removes cognitive friction when every second counts.
